name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea cleared near $535 a tonne for November, up 17% since September as gas supply to plants was cut 20%
state: Egyptian granular urea for November cleared at about $535 a tonne FOB, up about 17% from $457 in September, after gas supplies to some plants were cut by 20% from 1 Nov (EnterpriseAM, 4 Nov). Other Middle East origins were near $450 and India's October tender drew offers as low as $352 CFR. No rise of 60% in three months was found and the Hormuz route is impeded rather than closed, so the Alert is unconfirmed and Watch holds.
for_you: Higher fertiliser costs can feed into farm input prices and, later, food prices. Farmers buying for spring application and import-dependent countries are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Hormuz disruption restricting Gulf supply; urea rise below 60% in three months

sources.title: EnterpriseAM — Egyptian granular urea at USD 535 as gas supplies to fertilizer plants cut 20%

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
